sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Establishment**: Appointed in 1925, submitted report in 1926 to address the instability of the **Rupee-Sterling exchange rate**.
• **Core Recommendation**: Advocated for the creation of a **Central Bank** (Reserve Bank of India) to separate currency control from the government.
• **Gold Standard**: Recommended the adoption of the **Gold Bullion Standard** instead of the Gold Exchange Standard to ensure monetary autonomy.
• **Key Metric**: The commission suggested fixing the Rupee at **1s 6d (18 pence)**, a controversial move that sparked nationalist criticism for overvaluing the Rupee.

items.definition: A system where the currency is not convertible into gold coins, but the central bank is obligated to buy and sell gold bars (bullion) at fixed prices to maintain exchange rates.
The exchange rate of 1 Rupee = 18 pence. Nationalist leaders like Purushottamdas Thakurdas argued for 1s 4d, claiming 1s 6d hurt Indian exports and favored British imports.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **RBI Act 1934**: The direct legislative outcome of the Commission's recommendations.
• **Monetary Autonomy**: Shifted control from the Secretary of State for India to a domestic central authority.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Nationalist Opposition**: The '1s 6d' ratio was viewed as a 'drain of wealth' mechanism.
• **Institutional Transition**: The Imperial Bank of India struggled to relinquish its quasi-central banking functions.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'H-R-G' (Hilton-RBI-Gold).
• **Decoded Meaning**: Hilton Young Commission -> Recommended RBI -> Established Gold Bullion Standard.

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often confuses the Hilton Young Commission (1926) with the Fowler Committee (1898). Remember: Fowler = Gold Standard; Hilton Young = RBI/Central Bank.
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Monetary Sovereignty' when discussing the transition from the Imperial Bank to the RBI as recommended by the Commission.

keyTakeaways: The Hilton Young Commission is the primary architect of the Reserve Bank of India.
The 1s 6d exchange rate was a major point of contention between the colonial government and Indian nationalists.
It marked the end of the Gold Exchange Standard and the move toward a more centralized, bullion-backed monetary system.
